messages.subject: Estimators for non-normal data
parts:
Hello!
I need some help and I hope I'm in the right place.
I have non-normal data (items are continuous on a 9-point scale, but not normally distributed) and I want to conduct a confirmatory factor analysis in lavaan. I am aware that there are several robust options (MLM, MLMVS, MLMV, MLF, MLR) available for the estimators, but I'm not sure which one to use and how to make that decision.
Could anyone give me some guidelines, please?
Thank you a lot in advance!

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Estimators for non-normal data
parts: I am aware that there are several robust options (MLM, MLMVS, MLMV, MLF, MLR) available for the estimators, but I'm not sure which one to use and how to make that decision. Could anyone give me some guidelines, please?

I usually default to MLR because it is the most general, in that it can be applied when there are missing data and you want to use FIML.  Even with complete data, it is asymptotically equivalent to MLM, which may be preferable in smaller samples with no missing data.

Since this is not lavaan-specific, you can post your question on SEMNET if you want more information about the adjustments.

Terrence D. Jorgensen

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Estimators for non-normal data
parts: I was under the impression that FIML can be used only with ML - so it is ok if I use it with MLR, too?

MLR is ML.  The point estimates are the same.  After ML point and SE estimates are found, the SEs and chi-squared are adjusted by the amount of excess kurtosis.  Since FIML supplies that information, MLR can be used to adjust those SEs and chi-squared as well.
